'''John Friedlander''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}} is a [[Canadians|Canadian]] [[mathematician]] specializing in [[analytic number theory]]. He received his B.Sc. from the [[University of Toronto]] in 1965, an M.A. from the [[University of Waterloo]] in 1966, and a Ph.D. from [[Pennsylvania State University]] in 1972. He was a lecturer at [[M.I.T.]] in 1974–1976, and has been on the faculty of the [[University of Toronto]] since 1977, where he served as [[Chair (academic)|Chair]] during 1987–1991. He has also spent several years at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]]. In addition to his individual work, he has been notable for his collaborations with other well-known number theorists, including Enrico Bombieri, [[William Duke (mathematician)|William Duke]], [[Andrew Granville]], and especially [[Henryk Iwaniec]].<ref>{{cite web |title=John B. Friedlander (Toronto) |url=http://crm.math.ca/prix/prixCRMFieldsPIMS/prix_CFPFriedlander_an.shtml |publisher=Centre de recherches mathématiques |access-date=December 5, 2021}}</ref>

In 1997, in joint work with [[Henryk Iwaniec]], Friedlander proved that infinitely many [[prime numbers]] can be obtained as the sum of a square and fourth power: {{math|1=''a''<sup>2</sup> + ''b''<sup>4</sup>}}.<ref>{{cite journal|last = Friedlander|first = John|author2=Iwaniec, Henryk|title = The polynomial ''X''<sup>2</sup> + ''Y''<sup>4</sup> captures its primes|journal = Annals of Mathematics|volume = 148|year = 1998|pages = 945–1040|url = http://www.emis.de/journals/Annals/148_3/fried1.pdf|doi = 10.2307/121034|jstor = 121034|issue = 3|arxiv = math/9811185|s2cid = 1187277}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Friedlander |first1=John |last2=Iwaniec |first2=Henryk |year=1997 |title=Using a parity-sensitive sieve to count prime values of a polynomial |journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|PNAS]] |volume=94 |issue=4 |pages=1054–1058 |doi=10.1073/pnas.94.4.1054 |pmid=11038598 |pmc=19742|bibcode=1997PNAS...94.1054F |doi-access=free }}.</ref> Friedlander and Iwaniec improved [[Enrico Bombieri]]'s "asymptotic sieve" technique to construct their proof.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/ams/press/prime1.html International Team Shows that Primes Can Be Found in Surprising Places]</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* In 1999, Friedlander received the [[Jeffery–Williams Prize]].
* In 1988, Friedlander became a fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]].<ref>[http://rsc-src.ca/en/search-fellows Search Royal Society of Canada Fellows] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200204103715/https://rsc-src.ca/en/search-fellows |date=February 4, 2020 }}, retrieved 2013-01-2013.</ref>
* In 2002, [[CRM-Fields-PIMS prize]]
* In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref name="American Mathematical Society 2018 u222">{{cite web | title=Fellows of the American Mathematical Society | website=American Mathematical Society | date=November 26, 2018 | url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi | access-date=October 14, 2023}}</ref>
* In 2017, he received the [[Joseph L. Doob prize]], jointly with Henryk Iwaniec, for their book ''Opera de Cribro''.<ref name="American Mathematical Society 2018 t179">{{cite web | title=Joseph L. Doob Prize | website=American Mathematical Society | date=November 26, 2018 | url=http://www.ams.org/prizes-awards/paview.cgi?parent_id=21 | access-date=October 14, 2023}}</ref>
